--- sidebar_position: 7 title: Batch Workflows --- # Batch Workflows with TestGroup `TestGroup` holds labelled collections of objects (GOOD / BAD / ANY) so you can clean, analyse, and visualise many stars with one call instead of a manual loop. ::: {.cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from varistar import TimeSeries, LightCurve, TestGroup from _synthetic import make_sinusoidal_lightcurve lightcurves = [] for i, seed in enumerate([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]): df = make_sinusoidal_lightcurve(period=2.0 + 0.3 * i, seed=seed) ts = TimeSeries(magnitude="mag I", time_scale="HJD") ts.load_data_from_df(df, data_id=f"star_{i:03d}") ts.clean_by_error(max_error=0.05) lightcurves.append(LightCurve(ts)) group = TestGroup(good_ts=lightcurves[:4], bad_ts=lightcurves[4:], name="synthetic_sample") group.summary() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [clean_by_error] Removed 0 points (err > 0.05). TestGroup 'synthetic_sample' | GOOD: 4 BAD: 2 ANY/LC: 0 (total: 6) ``` ::: ::: ## Bulk period-finding `apply()` calls an *unbound* method on every registered object. `find_best_period` also fills in `is_harmonic`, which we'll use below: ::: {.cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} group.apply(LightCurve.find_best_period) ``` ::: ## Mosaic view ::: {.cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} group.plot_mosaic(LightCurve.plot_phased, n_cols=3, fit_model="fourier") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](batch-testgroup_files/figure-markdown_strict/cell-4-output-1.png){width=1145 height=565} ::: ::: ## Filtering and export ::: {.cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} short_period = group.filter_by("periods", lambda p: p[0] < 3.0, target="any") short_period.summary() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` TestGroup 'synthetic_sample[filtered]' | GOOD: 0 BAD: 0 ANY/LC: 4 (total: 4) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} group.export_periods() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
